blinding_guess.why: The package is the rosidl Python generator. It names none of the three elements, so any link to them would be indirect: it generates the Python class for std_msgs/String and the C conversion of its string field .data through resource/_msg.py.em and resource/_msg_support.c.em. Nothing I read shows a defect for these elements, and without further investigation I cannot tell whether the generated binding misbehaves for them.

notes: All three packet elements have side 'consumes'. By the rules, declares and not_declared cover only provided elements, so both stay empty. A consumed element goes into references only when the code names it; this snapshot names none of them, so references is empty and ports is empty because the package publishes, subscribes to, and calls none of them. Its only relation to std_msgs/String is as the generator that would be run on that message's definition when some other package builds it; the snapshot does not name that type. No dependency definition file was fetched because the snapshot's definitions and code do not depend on std_msgs, so no definition_id was computed. QoS, frame, units and rates do not apply because there are no ports. exclusive is empty: grep -i 'exclusive' matched only the license text.
